title: Passive selling: turn social attention into asset sales via a hook-body-CTA-article micro-funnel
summary: Justin lays out a data-driven system for keeping digital product sales going after launch without hard-selling on social. Track hooks, body copy and CTAs to find winning combos, send traffic to relevant articles instead of the homepage, and end each article with a soft CTA to the product.

principles.text: Post-launch sales longevity, not the launch, is what makes a digital asset valuable.
principles.quote: while having a successful course or book launch is important, maintaining sales (post-launch) is what makes an asset so valuable.

principles.text: Skip the hard sell on social; get enough relevant people in front of your product without saying 'buy this'.
principles.quote: there’s a better way to ‘sell’ without actually asking people to buy in your social content.

principles.text: Move people from short-form social to your website, where you can educate them on the problem.
principles.quote: my process is to get people to my website, where I can further educate them on the problem they’re trying to solve.

principles.text: Break social content into hook, body and CTA, and track each: the hook drives most impressions.
principles.quote: The hook on your social content is generally what leads to 90% of your success in terms of impressions

principles.text: After 3-6 months of publishing, identify your top five hooks, bodies and CTAs and combine the winners.
principles.quote: After three to six months of publishing content, you should have a good sense of your top five hooks, body styles, and calls-to-action.

principles.text: Send traffic to relevant articles, not the homepage, and end each with a passive CTA to your asset; rotate ~20 articles and track reader-to-buyer conversion.
principles.quote: These articles are like 24/7/365 salespeople that cost you nothing other than the time it takes to write them.
